department: College of Graduate Studies — Ph.D. in Neuroscience

deadline.value: Application opens September 1, 2026 and the final deadline is December 1, 2026.
deadline.quote: Application Timeline | Opens: Sept. 1, 2026 | Final deadline: Dec. 1, 2026

gre_subject.value: No ETS GRE Subject Test exists specifically for Neuroscience, and standardized test scores are not required.
gre_subject.quote: Submission of a standardized test score is not required but will be considered if submitted.

also.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

supervisor.value: No supervisor is required prior to admission; students complete laboratory rotations to choose a lab and faculty mentor.
supervisor.quote: How do students choose a lab or mentor? | You’ll use laboratory rotations and early research experiences to explore faculty research, mentoring styles and potential dissertation directions. These rotation experiences help you identify the lab environment and mentor that best aligns with your research interests and career goals.

funding.value: Students in the Ph.D. in Neuroscience program receive a $39,000 annual stipend (effective July 1, 2026) plus full coverage of tuition, fees, and health insurance.
funding.quote: Students in the Ph.D. in Neuroscience program at MUSC receive a $39,000 annual stipend, effective July 1, 2026. The program also covers tuition, fees and health insurance for these students.

entry_route.value: Applicants must possess or expect to earn a bachelor’s degree from an accredited U.S. institution or foreign equivalent prior to enrolling.
entry_route.quote: Possess, or expect to have earned, a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution in the U.S. or its equivalent from a foreign institution prior to enrolling

notes: Includes four research tracks: Addiction Neuroscience, Neurodegenerative Disease, Neurodevelopmental Disorders, and Neuro-Oncology.
